scope_statement: These measurements concern a SMALL-SCALE, AES-SHAPED cipher with n-bit cells (n = 3, 4, 5) and a 4x4 cell state, defined in gate_601b_impl.c. It is NOT AES. Nothing recorded here is a statement about AES at any round count, about full-round AES, or about the security of any deployed system. No literature comparison, recalled baseline, bit-margin, sota_delta, 8-bit extrapolation, or crossover prediction is made or implied anywhere in this record: per DEC-20260731-011 disposition CAND_601_B those are STRUCK, and the only baseline here is the direct partial-sums aggregation re-implemented in this same task and actually run on the same inputs. The original GATE-601-B PASS/FAIL escalation criterion is WITHDRAWN by the dispatching handoff and is not applied. This record reports observations only; it assigns no evidence strength, advances no hypothesis, and changes no official state.

experiment_definition.cipher: Small-scale AES-shaped SPN: n-bit cells over GF(2^n), 4x4 cell state, 5 rounds. X = P + K0; rounds 1-3 = SubCells, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey; round 4 = SubCells, ShiftRows, MixColumns (NO AddRoundKey); round 5 = SubCells, ShiftRows, AddRoundKey (NO MixColumns).
definitional_choices_declared: Round 4 carries no AddRoundKey. This is a deliberate simplification of the scaled cipher, made so that the key-guess space is EXACTLY the 4 cells specified for this gate (q^4 = 2^16 at n = 4) rather than 5 cells. It is a property of this toy construction and is not an AES round structure.
Round keys are 6 independent seeded random 16-cell keys; there is no key schedule.

MixColumns is the AES-shaped circulant (2,3,1,1) over GF(2^n) where that matrix satisfies three acceptance conditions (all entries nonzero; invertible; row 0 of the inverse has four nonzero pairwise-distinct entries). It does at n = 4 and n = 5. At n = 3 it does not, because its inverse row over GF(2^3) is (5,0,6,2) - a zero coefficient would make one guessed cell irrelevant and a repeated coefficient would make two guessed cells interchangeable - so at n = 3 the program deterministically uses the first circulant row in packed order that does satisfy the conditions, namely (5,2,1,1) with inverse row (7,4,2,5). Recorded per run in the raw measurements.

The 'algebraic' S-box is GF(2^n) inversion followed by an invertible GF(2)-affine map (smallest circulant tap mask that is invertible, plus the constant 0x63 & (2^n - 1)). At n = 3 the only invertible circulant tap masks have weight 1, so the affine layer there is the identity rotation; recorded as affine_taps in the raw measurements.
experiment_definition.data: Per structure: q^4 chosen plaintexts varying the four state-diagonal cells over all values with the other 12 cells constant - a disjoint union of q^3 Lambda-sets, so the 3-round balance property makes the aggregate zero for the correct guess. 5 structures per run. Reduced to a parity table N0 over the four ciphertext cells the guess acts on, at positions (row i, col (4-i) mod 4).
experiment_definition.aggregation_object: g(k) = XOR over the structure of Sinv( XOR_i G_i[c_i XOR k_i] ), G_i[y] = Minv[0][i] * Sinv(y). A guess k survives a structure iff g(k) = 0, and survives the run iff it survives all 5 structures.
experiment_definition.direct_implementation: Partial-sums aggregation: peels one ciphertext cell at a time, carrying a parity table that shrinks by a factor q per peeled cell (q^4 -> q^4 -> q^3 -> q^2 -> q), evaluated over the whole guess space.
experiment_definition.reorganized_implementation: The same g computed as a 4-dimensional Walsh-Hadamard convolution over the group (GF(2)^n)^4: for each of the n basis output-bit masks u, C_u = WHT^-1( WHT(N0) . WHT(F_u) ) with F_u(x) = (-1)^<u, Sinv(XOR_i G_i[x_i])>, and the survival bit recovered as ((T - C_u(k))/2) mod 2 with T = sum_c N0[c] = WHT(N0)[0].

classes.table_lookups: one indexed read of any array - lookup table or working table alike
classes.xors: one XOR of a data value or of an index value
classes.adds: one integer addition or subtraction on a data value
classes.muls: one integer multiplication on a data value

counting_convention.unweighted_caveat: The four classes are summed with weight 1 each. The two implementations have different op-class mixes - the direct side is lookups and XORs with zero adds, the reorganized side is lookups and adds plus one multiply per transformed entry - so a different per-class weighting would give a different ratio. The per-class breakdown is recorded so any weighting can be recomputed from these numbers.
not_counted_on_either_side: shifts and masks used for bit-field packing
outside_both_counters: construction of the parity tables N0
symmetry_demonstration: All counted sites on both sides go through the same four macros C_TL, C_XR, C_AD, C_ML, defined once at the top of gate_601b_impl.c and incremented through a single global counter pointer CUR that is retargeted per implementation.

The G_i table construction is literally the SAME function build_G(), called by both agg_direct() and agg_reorg(). Its standalone cost is measured separately and emitted per run as ops_shared_build_G: it is 4q table lookups and 4q multiplies - 64+64 at n=4 - and appears with exactly that value inside both totals. ops_direct_precompute_total equals it exactly (the direct side has no other precomputation).

Both implementations consume the SAME parity tables N0 for the same key, the same structures and the same S-box, and both sweep the FULL guess space for every structure; neither prunes using another structure's survivors.
Neither side's counters depend on the other's; each aggregation is run with its own zeroed counter struct.
counting_convention.residual_data_dependence: The reorganized side is fully data-oblivious: its counted total is EXACTLY constant across all keys and all S-box variants at a given cell width (verified: ops_reorg_total_constant_across_keys is true at every width and variant). The direct side has exactly one data-dependent counted site - the final aggregation step XORs Sinv(z) only for the odd-parity entries of the last table - so its total varies slightly with the data. That variation is present BETWEEN KEYS UNDER A FIXED S-BOX as well, and is what the null-control comparison below is measured against.

yield_1_correctness_equivalence.question: Do the reorganized and direct aggregations return the IDENTICAL surviving-key set on the same inputs?
yield_1_correctness_equivalence.protocol: Both aggregations run on the same N0 tables for every (cell width, S-box variant, key). The surviving-key bitmaps are compared byte-for-byte over the whole guess space with memcmp, and an FNV-1a-64 digest of each bitmap is recorded.
yield_1_correctness_equivalence.verdict_statement: In all 54 measurement runs - 24 of them at the fully enumerable 2^16 guess space, covering 8 distinct keys under each of the three S-box variants - the two aggregations returned byte-identical surviving-key bitmaps and identical digests, and the correct key survived under both. No VOID-by-disagreement condition was encountered.

yield_2_sbox_independence_null_control.question: The reorganization is algebraically S-box-agnostic, so the counted-operation ratio must not depend on the S-box. Does it?
yield_2_sbox_independence_null_control.null_object: The cipher's algebraic S-box replaced by a freshly drawn random bijection on the cell alphabet (Fisher-Yates over seeded splitmix64). TWO independent draws were used, A and B, with the seeds recorded above. Everything else - cipher structure, MixColumns, key seeds, structure seeds, both implementations and the counting convention - is unchanged.
yield_2_sbox_independence_null_control.verdict_statement: At every cell width the counted ratio under the two random-bijection null S-boxes differs from the ratio under the algebraic S-box by a relative amount far inside the 1% tolerance: 1.48e-05 at n=3, 7.69e-08 at n=4, 3.03e-08 at n=5. The reorganized side's counted total is EXACTLY invariant - bit-for-bit the same integer for every key and every S-box at a given width - and all of the residual movement is on the direct side's single data-dependent counted site. At n=4 and n=5 the between-S-box difference is SMALLER than the key-to-key spread observed within a single fixed S-box (7.69e-08 vs 6.00e-06 at n=4; 3.03e-08 vs 2.84e-07 at n=5), i.e. changing the S-box moves the ratio less than changing the key does under a fixed S-box. At n=3 the between-S-box difference (1.48e-05) is comparable to the within-S-box key-to-key spread (1.24e-04) and remains an order of magnitude smaller than it. No VOID-by-S-box-dependence condition was encountered.
yield_2_sbox_independence_null_control.artifact_check: A ratio that MOVED under S-box randomization would have proved the measured difference an implementation artifact rather than an algebraic property, and would have been reported as VOID. It did not move beyond the stated tolerance, so that VOID condition did not fire. This is a statement about these two implementations at these cell widths and nothing more.

yield_3_measured_counted_ratio.verdict_statement: Measured counted-operation ratio (reorganized total / direct total, unweighted, over the full 5-structure key-recovery task): 0.10651 at 3-bit cells (guess space 2^12), 0.044370 at 4-bit cells (guess space 2^16), 0.016585 at 5-bit cells (guess space 2^20). Each number is the mean over all keys and all three S-box variants actually run at that width; the spread across those runs is at most 1.6e-04 relative. These are measurements at the widths run. No scaling law is fitted to them, no crossover is predicted, and nothing is extrapolated to any other cell width.

additional_observations_recorded_not_int: At 3-bit cells the surviving-key set does not shrink to the correct key: it saturates at roughly 30 of the 4096 guesses (observed range 29-37 across the 24 declared runs at that width) and stops shrinking as structures are added. Exact numbers from the exploratory development sweep, one value per S-box variant at key index 0: BEFORE the MixColumns acceptance rule was introduced (first row (2,3,1,1), whose inverse row over GF(2^3) is (5,0,6,2) with a zero coefficient, making one guessed cell irrelevant) the survivor counts at 1,2,3,4,5,6 structures were (640,736,672), (272,328,312), (232,216,224), (192,184,192), (176,176,176), (176,176,176); AFTER the rule (first row (5,2,1,1), inverse row (7,4,2,5)) they were (608,576,552) at 1 structure, (45,42,51) at 3, (30,32,32) at 5 and (30,29,31) at 6. The correct key is always among the survivors and both implementations always agree on the whole set. This is recorded as an unexplained property of the 8-element cell alphabet in this toy construction. It is not investigated further because it lies outside the three yields, and it does not affect them: the equivalence check compares whatever sets arise, and the counted ratio is not a function of the survivor count on either side.
At 4-bit and 5-bit cells the surviving-key set is the correct key alone in 44 of the 48 runs at those widths, with 3 runs returning 2 survivors and 1 run returning 3.

The direct side records zero counted additions and the reorganized side records only 1082368 counted XORs at n=5 against 760217600 counted additions; the two op-class profiles are genuinely different, which is why the unweighted-total caveat above is stated explicitly.

The reorganized side's precomputation - the G tables, the combined table Z, and the transformed mask functions - is independent of the key and of the data structures, so it is paid once per cipher, while the direct side's precomputation is only the shared G tables. Both parts of that split are reported as measured numbers in cost_decomposition_example_run; no model is fitted to them.

protocol_deviations: The number of keys is 8 per S-box variant at 3-bit and 4-bit cells but 2 per variant at 5-bit cells, because a 5-bit run costs about 40 s per key-variant and the full sweep had to fit the 2700 s budget. The completion gate requires at least 8 keys at the 2^16 guess space (4-bit cells); that requirement is met with 8 distinct keys under each of the three S-box variants, 24 runs. The 3-bit and 5-bit widths are measurements, not the gated instance.

At 3-bit cells the MixColumns first row is (5,2,1,1) rather than the AES-shaped (2,3,1,1), for the recorded algebraic reason above. This is a property of the toy cipher at that width and is recorded per run rather than hidden.

Development iterations were run in the scratchpad before the declared runs, including an exploratory survivor-count sweep and a first version whose 3-bit MixColumns inverse row had a zero coefficient. They are described in run_record.md rather than discarded. No declared run was repeated to obtain a more favourable number, and the declared measurement run was executed exactly once.

raw_measurements.counting_convention: TL=indexed array read; XR=XOR of a data or index value; AD=integer add/sub on a data value; ML=integer multiply on a data value; total=TL+XR+AD+ML. Not counted on either side: array writes, memset, loop bookkeeping, shifts/masks for bit-field packing, comparisons and branches. Shared preprocessing outside both counters: key setup, S-box construction, encryption, construction of the parity tables N0.
